sections.h2: Where to record a deed in Franklin County
sections.html:
Deeds are recorded by the Franklin County Register & Recorder at the Administration Building, 272 North Second Street, Chambersburg, PA 17201. The phone is 717-261-3872 and the fax is 717-709-7211.

One office wears several hats. Besides land records, deeds and mortgages, it handles probate for executors and administrators, records military discharges, and collects Pennsylvania realty transfer tax and inheritance tax for the Department of Revenue.

A deed signed at a Franklin County closing finishes its trip here. Once recorded, it becomes part of the land record that every later buyer, lender and title agent searches.

The county accepts deeds by e-recording through Simplifile, CSC or EPN, by mail, or in person at the Chambersburg office. Hours are 8:30 a.m. to 4:30 p.m., Monday through Friday. The office is closed on weekends and county-observed holidays.

Searching is done remotely through Landex. For questions about that system, call 717-274-5890. Probate filings are by appointment only, but recording doesn't need one.

  • E-recording: Simplifile, CSC or EPN, with electronic rejection notices that explain the reason.
  • Mail or overnight delivery: rejected documents come back unrecorded with a written explanation.
  • In person: the clerk reviews the document at the counter before it is accepted.

Whichever route you use, the county scans the document and sends it to the Tax Assessment Office for UPI certification. It then returns to the recorder for recording, and the UPI stamp prints on the ending page. A document with a missing or wrong parcel number is returned with a note on what to fix.

A deed or a mortgage is $92.75 on the schedule posted for July 2026, and every document is priced at four pages and four names. The listed fees already include one UPI certification. Each extra certification adds $20.00.

Franklin County fees for common home-sale documents
DocumentRecording fee
Deed$92.75
Deed of distribution (Statement of Value required)$92.75
Mortgage$92.75
Satisfaction of mortgage$81.75
Assignment$81.75
Easement (Statement of Value required)$79.75
Power of attorney to sell real estate$38.50
Statement of Value$1.00

Beyond those, each page past four costs $2.00 and each name past four costs $0.50. Copies are $0.25 per page, copies of subdivisions $0.50, and certification of a document $1.50.

A state tax of 1% and a local tax of the same amount are due at recording, so the combined rate is 2% of the price, or of the assessed value where no price applies.

Every deed must either state the true consideration or carry a Statement of Value. If a full or partial exemption is claimed, the Statement of Value is mandatory unless the deed itself notes the exemption, and it must be fully completed. Corrective deeds and any deed recorded more than 30 days after signing also need one.

  • A deed of distribution from an estate requires a Statement of Value.
  • A property in two or more taxing districts must show the value in each district on the deed so the local share lands in the right place.
  • Pennsylvania lists family transfers, transfers by will or intestacy, and transfers to government units among the exempt categories.

Grantor and grantee are jointly and severally liable, so an unpaid tax can reach either side of a Franklin County sale.

sections.h2: Selling a house that came through an estate
sections.html:
The same office that records the deed also opens the estate, so an heir can handle both in Chambersburg. Probating needs an appointment. The deed that moves title out of the estate is recorded as a deed of distribution with a Statement of Value attached.

Register of Wills fees step up with the size of the estate. Letters and probate run $30.00 for an estate up to $1,000 and $80.00 for one between $75,001 and $100,000, then $35.00 for each additional $100,000 or fraction. Probate also carries a $5.00 automation fee and a $41.25 JCP fee.

  • Short certificates are $5.00 each, and a lender or bank often asks for one.
  • An inheritance tax return or supplemental return is $20.00.
  • Certification of inheritance tax paid is $5.00.
  • An inventory and appraisement is $10.00.

Because the county collects Pennsylvania inheritance tax through this office, an heir who intends to sell the inherited house can finish the estate paperwork and the recording at one counter.

The deed is the main document, but a few others turn up around a sale. Releasing a loan is recorded as a satisfaction or release of mortgage at $81.75, and a partial release costs the same.

Leases are $38.50 unless they run 30 years, which needs a Statement of Value and costs $79.75. A right of way is $78.75, an installment sales agreement $79.75, and a memorandum $38.50. Farm owners may also record an Ag Security Map at $35.00, and plans on 8.5 by 14 paper are $35.00.

If you had a prior mortgage, confirm before closing that its satisfaction was recorded. A loan that was paid off but never released can still show up in a title search.

sections.h2: Free record alerts for your parcel
sections.html:
The Recorder of Deeds offers a free Landex Record Alert. It notifies an owner when a document carrying their parcel number is recorded or corrected. Sign-up is by email address or mobile number.

The service keys on the parcel number, which is 20 characters including dots and dashes and appears on a tax bill. The county calls the alert a courtesy tool. It doesn't replace your own diligence, paid monitoring or a lawyer. If you suspect fraud, contact local law enforcement quickly.

Signing up before you list is a cheap check. You can see any mortgage, easement or release recorded against the parcel while a sale is pending.

Franklin County has an estimated 160,652 residents as of July 2025, up 3.0% from the April 2020 base. The median owner-occupied home is worth $249,800 for 2020 to 2024, and owners occupy 73.5% of housing. Chambersburg sits at the center of the county.

Whoever sells a Franklin County house finishes at the Chambersburg office, so the deed paperwork above is the last item to confirm with the closing agent. A cash sale skips the lender's steps, but the recording requirements stay the same. Ask whether the deed will go out by e-recording or by mail, because that choice decides how fast you get the recorded copy back.

faqs.q: How much is the UPI certification in Franklin County?
faqs.a: The first certification is built into the listed recording fee. Each additional UPI certification is $20.00, so a deed covering two parcels adds $20.00 to the posted price.

faqs.q: Can I e-record a deed in Franklin County?
faqs.a: Yes. The Register & Recorder accepts e-recording through Simplifile, CSC or EPN, plus mail and in-person submissions at the Chambersburg office.

faqs.q: What is the Statement of Value fee in Franklin County?
faqs.a: It is $1.00. You need one when a deed claims a transfer tax exemption, when a deed is corrective or recorded after 30 days, and for deeds of distribution.

faqs.q: When is the Franklin County recorder open?
faqs.a: Monday through Friday, 8:30 a.m. to 4:30 p.m. The office is closed on weekends and county-observed holidays. Probate filings need an appointment.

faqs.q: Who do I call about the Landex search system in Franklin County?
faqs.a: Call 717-274-5890 for Landex questions. The main line at 717-261-3872 handles recording, fees and probate appointments.
